Chapter 1 — Daughter of the Earth:
Light filtered through the treetops like golden fingers, caressing the leaf-covered ground. The air carried the moist scent of earth, mingled with the subtle aroma of freshly gathered medicinal plants. There, in the heart of the forest, time did not pass — it breathed.

Yaraúna, only eight years old, sat cross-legged before her grandmother, Kuara, the village healer. The girl's eyes were fixed on the elder's hands, which moved calmly and ceremoniously to sort healing leaves.

"This one is urucumã," Kuara murmured, her voice deep and serene. "It warms the chest when sorrow enters."

Yaraúna did not speak. Silence was the language of the forest. And in silence, she learned.

She watched every movement with reverence. Her black hair fell over her small shoulders, her bare feet lightly pressed into the soil. She was one with the forest, as if shaped there among vines and roots. Her gaze, though young, already held the depth of one who understood that nature was not mere backdrop — it was spirit.

Kuara lifted the bundle of leaves toward her granddaughter.

"You have the gift of listening, my wind-flower. One day, your voice will guide those who are lost."

The sun tilted toward the horizon, coloring the forest in shades of orange and red. The birds gradually quieted, as if they, too, were listening.

Little Yaraúna reached out and received the leaves gently. Her eyes met her grandmother's, and in that moment, the whole forest seemed to hold its breath.

She didn’t know it yet, but in that simple gesture was born the path of a woman who would become a bridge between worlds.

And the wind, an old accomplice, whispered through the trees: she was a daughter of the earth. And the earth never forgets its own.
